# @cesarus777/opencode-censor

A native OpenCode V2 server plugin that asks a separately selected model to review shell permissions before execution. The model can recommend `allow` or `ask`; OpenCode executes the action and owns the approval interface. The plugin contains no shell executor, agent, terminal, backend, or approval UI.

Release 0.3.1 targets **OpenCode / `@opencode/plugin` 2.2.5** and defaults to a small set of inspection commands. This is a security-sensitive initial release candidate. Package import and mocked integration are distinct from a live provider test; see [verification](docs/VERIFICATION.md) and [SDK research](docs/RESEARCH.md).

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T[Native shell tool input] --> C[Capture input by session, message and call ID]
  C --> R[OpenCode permission rules]
  R -->|explicit deny| D[OpenCode blocks action]
  R -->|allow or ask| H[Permission evaluate hook]
  H --> P[Check full input, resources and local policy]
  P -->|stateless inspection| L[Stateless independent model generation]
  P -->|opt-in stateful| G[Bounded project evidence and reviewer loop]
  G --> V
  P -->|unsafe or incomplete| A[Set ask]
  L --> V[Strict JSON validation and final local policy]
  V -->|valid low-risk allow| E[Set allow]
  V -->|ask, error, ambiguity or timeout| A
  A --> U[Native OpenCode manual approval]
  U --> X[OpenCode continues or rejects]
  E --> X
```

The `tool.execute.before` hook only observes input. The `permission.evaluate` hook changes the decision. Both are native V2 hooks. Explicit configured denies are final before evaluation. Other permission actions pass through untouched.

Scanner resources may omit shell operators, redirections, or other parts of the source. Stateless automatic approval therefore requires a matching captured **complete** tool command, one identical scanner resource, and a command accepted by the local inspection grammar. Missing source identifiers, expired correlation, multiple resources, changed input, an external `workdir`, or unsupported shell syntax produce `ask`. A resource that happens to say `pwd` is insufficient on its own.

Version 0.2.0 also supports opt-in [stateful project review](docs/STATEFUL.md)
for generic commands with bounded, model-requested project evidence. Project review
delegates program semantics to the reviewer and enforces local evidence,
budget and approval constraints; it does not interpret build tools or languages. These options and custom reviewer instructions require version 0.2.0 or later.

## Install from npm

OpenCode can install the package directly from configuration; no source copying is needed:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "@cesarus777/opencode-censor@0.3.1",
      "options": {
        "model": { "providerID": "anthropic", "id": "MODEL_ID" },
      },
    },
  ],
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "git push *", "effect": "deny" },
    { "action": "external_directory", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
  ],
}
```

`MODEL_ID` is a placeholder: replace it with a model available in your OpenCode installation. A literal placeholder is rejected. Use `opencode models` to inspect available models and connect the provider through OpenCode. The reviewer uses existing OpenCode provider credentials; the plugin asks for no API keys. It never inherits the working agent's selected model implicitly. A different supported provider is valid.

For **global** activation, put the configuration in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. For **project** activation, put it in `<project>/opencode.jsonc` or `<project>/.opencode/opencode.jsonc`. Merge entries with existing configuration; do not duplicate the plugin. OpenCode's managed configuration and rule precedence still apply. Keep independent hard-deny rules for operations that must never run.

`@cesarus777/opencode-censor@0.3.1` adds hybrid routing, project subdirectory support and bounded project queues, retaining opt-in stateful review and provider checks. Publication status is recorded in [verification](docs/VERIFICATION.md). The earlier unscoped `opencode-censor` package is deprecated: replace its configuration entry with `@cesarus777/opencode-censor@0.3.1` and do not load both packages. The plugin ID remains `opencode-censor`. See [verification](docs/VERIFICATION.md) for publication status, accepted dependency risks and deferred deployment checks.

## Install local source or a tarball

Requires Bun 1.3.11 or later for development, and the compatible OpenCode V2 host. Node 22 or later is supported for importing the compiled ESM package.

```sh
cd /absolute/path/to/opencode-censor
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run check
```

Use the **package directory** in your OpenCode config:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "/absolute/path/to/opencode-censor",
      "options": {
        "model": { "providerID": "anthropic", "id": "MODEL_ID" },
      },
    },
  ],
  "permissions": [{ "action": "shell", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }],
}
```

The directory exports `dist/index.js`; run the build after editing source. OpenCode also accepts relative plugin directories and `file://` directory URLs.

To distribute a standalone archive:

```sh
bun run build
npm pack
npm install --prefix /path/to/plugins ./cesarus777-opencode-censor-0.3.1.tgz
```

Set `plugins[].package` to `/path/to/plugins/node_modules/@cesarus777/opencode-censor`. The installed package contains compiled JavaScript, declarations, license, documentation and examples; it does not require copying this repository into each project.

Version 0.3.1 implements the [development workflow plan](docs/DEVELOPMENT-WORKFLOW-PLAN.md): explicit hybrid review, project subdirectory working directories and bounded project review queues. Use [the development configuration](examples/opencode-development.jsonc) to select hybrid; the default remains stateless. See [verification](docs/VERIFICATION.md) for staging and public availability.

Hybrid routes an eligible closed-grammar inspection with matching complete source
and scanner resource to the existing stateless reviewer. It requires no project
file read. Other eligible commands use project evidence review. Both paths need a
fresh valid model decision; an inspection ask, error or timeout ends as ask and is
never retried through project review. `alwaysAsk` applies before routing. On the
hybrid inspection path, forbidding either `workspace_read` or `process_execution`
conservatively forces ask for every inspection, including `pwd`. Other effect
restrictions retain the existing inspection boundary and its trusted-host limits.
Hybrid requires `review.project.allowFileContents: true`; evidence scopes constrain
the project path, while inspection commands retain their documented grammar.
Explicit stateful review still requires full-file evidence even for inspections.

Native workdirs may be project subdirectories such as `packages/app`. The plugin
validates canonical containment and directory identities, rejects symlink components and native home-relative `~`/`~/…` spellings,
and rechecks the native workdir before allow. Evidence paths remain project-root-relative;
project prompts receive the actual relative workdir. Filesystem changes after the
final check remain possible. The original 2.2.5 scanner has been verified with
execution prevented; remote-provider and interactive-client acceptance remain separate.

## Configuration

Options are read once during setup from `ctx.options`. Reload the plugin after changing them. See [the complete example](examples/opencode.jsonc).

| Option                    | Default        | Contract                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`                 | `true`         | `false` delegates to OpenCode rules; a valid model configuration remains required                                                           |
| `model.providerID`        | required       | OpenCode provider ID, independent of the agent model                                                                                        |
| `model.id`                | required       | OpenCode model ID; no automatic fallback to another model                                                                                   |
| `mode`                    | `balanced`     | `strict`, `balanced`, or `permissive`                                                                                                       |
| `review.strategy`         | `stateless`    | `stateless` inspection, opt-in `stateful` project review, or `hybrid` routing; see [project options](docs/STATEFUL.md)                      |
| `systemPrompt`            | `""`           | Additional operator review instructions; at most 6000 characters; cannot override local policy                                              |
| `fallback`                | `ask`          | Only `ask` is supported                                                                                                                     |
| `timeoutMs`               | `15000`        | Integer 10–60000; covers source/directory checks, queue waiting, context, evidence, generation and rechecks together                        |
| `context.enabled`         | `false`        | Opt in to local extraction of task-intent labels                                                                                            |
| `context.maxMessages`     | `5`            | Inspect at most the last 1–20 returned context entries locally                                                                              |
| `context.maxCharacters`   | `6000`         | Scan at most 1–12000 characters of user text locally                                                                                        |
| `logging.enabled`         | `true`         | Write structured JSON audit records                                                                                                         |
| `logging.level`           | `info`         | `info`: all decisions; `error`: fallback records only                                                                                       |
| `logging.file`            | XDG state path | Absolute JSONL audit file path; defaults to `~/.local/state/opencode-censor/audit.jsonl` (or `$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode-censor/audit.jsonl`) |
| `logging.includeCommands` | `true`         | Include the exact captured shell command; set `false` to omit command text                                                                  |
| `cache.enabled`           | `false`        | Only `false` supported; no cached or transferable approvals                                                                                 |

Unknown keys, bad types, invalid bounds, unsupported sensitive options, or a missing model install a fail-safe hook that changes in-scope decisions to `ask`. Invalid configuration emits fixed metadata without echoing supplied values. Check `event.message` or audit records for `invalid_configuration`. Explicit `deny` and other permission actions remain unchanged.

### Custom reviewer instructions

`mode` sets the caution level: `strict`, `balanced` (default), or `permissive`.
Add `systemPrompt` to the existing plugin options for extra review instructions:

```json
{
  "mode": "strict",
  "systemPrompt": "Treat uncertain intent as suspicious. Ask whenever repository inspection could disclose sensitive information. Require clear evidence before recommending allow."
}
```

Keep the required `model` option alongside these fields. `systemPrompt` defaults to
an empty string and accepts at most 6000 characters, without NUL characters.
It is sent to your reviewer provider; do not put secrets in it. Reload after edits.
The pinned SDK accepts one prompt string, so this option supplements the built-in
instructions rather than creating a separate provider system message. It cannot
expand the selected strategy's local command grammar, replace its JSON response
contract, or bypass source checks. Custom instructions can request greater caution; a prompt asking
for broader approvals cannot make unsupported commands eligible.

## Decision criteria and modes

Every automatic approval needs **both** a valid model decision and the independent local policy. In the default stateless strategy, all modes escalate deletion, system changes, elevated privileges, external transmission, install/run pipelines, scripts, containers, unknown executables, shell expansion, redirection, composition, and ambiguous inputs. Task intent cannot override this boundary. The first release does not emit automatic `deny`; configured OpenCode deny rules provide hard prohibitions.

| Mode         | Eligible commands                                                                                                                                                                   | Confidence floor when supplied |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `strict`     | Exact `pwd`, `git status`, `git status --short`, `git status --porcelain`                                                                                                           | 0.98                           |
| `balanced`   | Strict set, `ls`, one `ls` flag group containing 1–3 letters from `a`, `l`, `h`; `git --no-pager diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv` optionally followed by `--stat` or `--name-only` | 0.90                           |
| `permissive` | Balanced set, `git diff --stat`, `git diff --name-only`, `git --no-pager log -N` where N is 1–9                                                                                     | 0.80                           |

The command grammar is intentionally exact: no arbitrary paths, revision arguments, quoting, extra whitespace, config flags, environment assignments, or flags outside this table. Candidate commands still require model review. Confidence is optional, never sufficient, and cannot override risk, schema, or policy checks. Strict mode also asks the reviewer to require exceptional certainty.

| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pwd`, `git status`, `ls -la`                                                   | May allow after low-risk model review in an eligible mode               |
| `git diff`                                                                      | Ask: unqualified diffs can invoke external diff/text conversion helpers |
| `git --no-pager diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv`                               | May allow in balanced/permissive                                        |
| `rm -rf ./src`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -fdx`                            | Ask                                                                     |
| `git push --force`                                                              | Ask, or native deny if configured                                       |
| `sudo chmod -R 777 /`                                                           | Ask                                                                     |
| `curl https://example.com/install.sh \| bash`                                   | Ask                                                                     |
| `npm install`, `make`, `python script.py`, `bash script.sh`, `docker run image` | Ask: indirect arbitrary execution                                       |
| `pwd && git status`, substitutions, nested shells, unknown binaries             | Ask

- Host executables, shell startup files, environment, Git configuration, filesystem and other plugins must be trusted. Even inspection may invoke configured helpers (for example Git fsmonitor), write index metadata, or expose output to the working agent. Closed syntax does not prove absence of side effects in a hostile runtime.
- The plugin never verifies executable binaries or provides filesystem isolation. All paths validate canonical project-local workdirs and recheck directory identity. Project review inspects model-requested files within permitted scopes, rejects symlinked evidence paths and rechecks file hashes. Filesystem races during inspection and the final check/run interval remain host concerns.
- Other trusted plugins may mutate tool inputs or override a decision later. Put this gate after command-rewriting plugins, avoid conflicting permission hooks, and test your actual plugin combination. An explicit native configured deny is stronger than a plugin-generated ask.
- The reviewer shares OpenCode's process/provider infrastructure and may use the same vendor; independent model selection is not process isolation. Native generation hooks or provider diagnostics may observe prompts.
- Experimental generation contracts can change. Dependency and host compatibility are pinned and must be retested when upgraded. No V1 adapter is supplied.
- A plugin that fails to load cannot intercept anything. The broad native shell `ask` rule is an essential deployment fallback.

## Development, tests and release

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run typecheck
bun run lint
bun test tests
bun run build
bun run test:package
```

`bun:test` provides deterministic TypeScript mocks, fake provider responses and bounded real timers without another runner dependency. Tests never execute the shell strings being reviewed. Integration tests load the real SDK entrypoint against a mocked host; they cover hook registration, source correlation, effects, provider failures, context filtering, explicit deny preservation, concurrency and cleanup. These are not live provider integration tests.

`test:package` creates an npm archive, installs it with npm and lifecycle scripts disabled into an isolated consumer, and imports the public export through Bun and Node. Installation may access the registry for dependencies. It requires subprocess execution and an available npm executable. Source maps/declarations are included; tests and probe code are not published. CI runs formatting, typecheck, tests, build and package validation.

Optional native host probe:

```sh
bun run build
OPENCODE_BIN=/absolute/path/to/opencode bun run test:live
```

This installs the npm archive into an isolated consumer and starts exactly OpenCode 2.2.5 with synthetic credentials and a controlled loopback HTTP provider. The test driver replaces the shell tool with permission assertions; no reviewed command is executed and no pending request is approved. It checks native source hooks, allow/ask/error/deny, tool completion, delayed and late replies, eight-request capacity, concurrent requests, reload, and the generic evidence loop with allow/ask/unavailable-file outcomes. It requires subprocess and loopback access. The native CI job pins Bun 1.3.11 and OpenCode 2.2.5 and needs no external provider credentials.

This command always uses the controlled loopback provider and consumes no remote-model allowance. The separate optional free-provider check below uses a remote service.

The separate original-scanner phase preserves the native shell tool, records the gate decision and forces native deny before process creation. Thirteen fixed fixtures cover exact inspections, flags, unsupported arguments, compounds, pipelines and subdirectory workdirs; see [the inspected hook order](docs/RESEARCH.md#original-225-scanner-and-pre-spawn-interception--2026-11-09). Real reviewer and interactive native-client acceptance remain mandatory; follow the [release checklist](docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md) and record evidence in [verification](docs/VERIFICATION.md). Provider cancellation is limited by the pinned SDK adapter even when native permission waiting is bounded.

Source and non-sensitive bug reports: [cesarus777/opencode-censor](https://github.com/cesarus777/opencode-censor). Security reports must follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Before publishing, complete or explicitly defer the checklist items, triage dependency advisories, confirm npm account access and inspect/install the final archive. Private reporting and deployment verification remain outstanding; the two moderate dependency advisories are explicitly accepted. `npm view` checks availability, not ownership. See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for release changes.

The build and test scripts do not stage or publish. The [staging workflow](.github/workflows/publish.yml) stages a verified archive when a stable version tag is pushed, or when manually run on `main` with the matching package version. It runs the full checks and native smoke, then inspects and installs the exact archive it stages with lifecycle scripts disabled. A maintainer must approve the staged package with 2FA on npm before it becomes public. For `0.3.1`, push tag `v0.3.1` or run the workflow manually on `main` with version `0.3.1`.

Before the first Actions publication, configure a GitHub Actions trusted publisher in the **scoped package's** npm Settings: owner `cesarus777`, repository `opencode-censor`, workflow filename `publish.yml`, and no environment name. A publisher configured for the old unscoped package does not transfer. Allow `npm stage publish` (enabled by default). The workflow uses Node 24, GitHub-hosted runners and OIDC; no `NPM_TOKEN` secret is needed. See [npm's trusted publishing instructions](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/).

For each release, update the package version, changelog and verification record, review outstanding dependency risks and deployment acceptance, and commit the release changes. Push the matching tag only when staging is intended; approve the staged package on npm to make it public. The scoped package starts at `0.1.0`; after its initial publication, use a new version for the next release. After npm approval, stable versions become available under `latest`; prerelease versions are rejected.

### Free-provider integration check

`bun run test:live:free` loads the installed archive into isolated OpenCode 2.2.5
and uses its built-in `opencode` provider for the reviewer. Select a model explicitly:

```sh
CENSOR_FREE_MODEL=YOUR_FREE_MODEL_ID OPENCODE_BIN=/absolute/path/to/opencode bun run test:live:free
```

Use Bun 1.3.11 or later on `PATH` (including for nested scripts) and build first.
The host catalog must report an enabled text model with explicit zero input,
output and cache prices in every pricing tier. Missing pricing, unavailable models
and paid models fail preflight; there is no model fallback. Catalog pricing is a
preflight check, not a billing guarantee. The check does not inherit account
credentials or personal host configuration. A model requiring authentication will
fail safely rather than use your saved account.

Only synthetic inspection input reaches the remote reviewer. A deterministic
loopback working model drives an inert replacement shell; reviewed commands never
execute and pending permissions are never answered. The suite checks missing
source, local policy ask, native deny, one real stateless reviewer decision and
reload cleanup. It reports fixed reason codes and exits unsuccessfully if the
reviewer cannot produce a valid automatic allow, including when a safe ask results
from provider errors, invalid JSON or timeout. The review deadline is 15 seconds;
a host watchdog stops the isolated process after two minutes. Native provider
retries and transport cancellation remain host controlled.

The **Free provider acceptance** GitHub workflow is manual and accepts a model ID.
It is separate from required deterministic CI. Free model availability changes;
model discovery and zero-price validation occur on each run. Stateful remote
review and interactive approval acceptance remain
separate from this check.

# Security policy

This plugin is a permission reviewer, not an execution sandbox. No absolute safety guarantee is made. Version 0.3.1 targets OpenCode 2.2.5; host and provider acceptance testing must be completed before relying on it in production.

## Threat model

The working agent may propose destructive, deceptive or ambiguous commands. Command arguments and task history may contain prompt injections, sensitive data, arbitrary executable names or hostile shell syntax. A reviewer may hallucinate, produce malformed output, time out or fail. Multiple permission evaluations may overlap, and providers may ignore cancellation.

The trusted computing base includes OpenCode's rule evaluation, scanner and permission machinery, this plugin and its dependencies, the selected provider, installed executables, shell startup/configuration, the workspace runtime, and other loaded plugins. The reviewer does not receive execution tools, but shares the OpenCode process and native generation infrastructure. Separate model selection is not a hard isolation boundary.

## Protections

- Explicit native deny rules run before hooks and remain authoritative. The plugin also defensively leaves incoming deny events untouched.
- In-scope existing allows are immediately downgraded before asynchronous review. Any review, configuration, parsing, context or timeout error produces ask.
- Stateless candidate commands must match a closed inspection grammar and a captured complete native shell tool input. Multiple scanner fragments, absent source IDs, changed source, expired correlation and unsupported workdirs ask.
- In stateless mode, free shell programs, redirection, substitutions, command chains, network operations, installation, scripts, privilege changes, deletion and history mutation never become automatic allow, even with a malicious allow response.
- The response parser rejects extra fields, nested values, duplicate keys, invalid values, unknown decisions and ambiguous/contradictory allow explanations. Risk, reason and local policy checks are independent of confidence.
- Only commands eligible for the configured local strategy cross the provider boundary. A sensitive-data tripwire supplements the grammar. Optional context transmits fixed intent labels rather than original text or file contents.
- Per-evaluation deadlines, lifecycle cancellation and a bound of eight unsettled tasks prevent indefinite UI waiting and unbounded model requests. Late results cannot change returned effects.
- Audit file records use fixed local reason/detail codes, stages, effective settings and bounded numeric diagnostics; see [the audit reference](docs/AUDIT.md). File write failures can make counts incomplete but cannot change a permission result. Records include native session IDs and, by default, exact captured commands. Commands can contain credentials, paths and other private data. Set `logging.includeCommands: false` to omit command text; disable logging to omit all audit records. Raw history, model output and error messages are not logged.

## Opt-in stateful project review

Stateful review deliberately delegates program semantics to a generic model loop.
It has no Make/Bash interpreters, command allowlists or trusted recipe steps. This
expands the original inspection-only boundary: local policy constrains disclosure,
observable command features, source correlation, budgets, validated declarations
and evidence freshness; it cannot independently prove arbitrary programs safe.

Explicit `allowFileContents` consent permits model-requested files within configured
project-relative path scopes to reach the selected provider. Raw history and
runtime environment values remain excluded. Read/list/literal-search operations
use bounded filesystem APIs only, with no subprocesses, execution tools or working
agents. Traversal, symlinks, protected paths, invalid encoding, sensitive matches
and exceeded limits produce unavailable evidence and prevent allow. Secret
tripwires are heuristic and cannot guarantee confidential data is removed.

A final allow needs a successful referenced current full-file read, no unresolved
evidence failures, low model risk, sufficient confidence, no declared uncertainty,
and no model-declared forbidden or unknown effects. These are model declarations,
not enforcement of all transitive effects. A lying or mistaken reviewer can
misjudge a harmful eligible command. Native hard denies remain authoritative.
Use actual host isolation for filesystem/network restrictions.

All inspected file contents and visible directory inventories are rechecked, as
are native input, project-local directory identity and scanner resources. Multiple scanner fragments
are supplemental only; the captured complete command is supplied independently.
Prior findings are withheld until their evidence is freshly reacquired and matches
its fingerprints. Temporary state is bounded, expires and never caches approvals.
Audit includes session IDs and optional exact commands, but no evidence file contents or provider prose.
See [the protocol, configuration and limits](docs/STATEFUL.md).

Hybrid keeps the default stateless grammar intact and never retries an inspection
ask through project review. It requires disclosure consent because other eligible
commands may acquire evidence. `alwaysAsk` applies to both paths; forbidding reads
or process execution conservatively blocks hybrid inspections. Stateful full-file
evidence requirements apply to the project path. Inspection relies on its narrower
source/resource grammar and reviewer contract and acquires no evidence files.

Native `~` and `~/…` workdirs are rejected before any evidence or model review,
even when a literal project directory with that name exists. This avoids confusing
OpenCode 2.2.5 home expansion with project-relative filesystem resolution.
Directory identity checks include canonical project containment and every workdir
component. Evidence scopes remain rooted at the project root. Findings and file
hints are separated by workdir. A directory or input change while queued or under
review cannot reuse an allow. A final filesystem check cannot close the check/run
race; trusted native shell hooks or other plugins can still change execution input.

Project reviews queue FIFO per session with 32 global/eight per-session waiters and
eight active or unsettled tasks. Total deadlines include waiting and final checks.
Timed-out operations keep capacity and session locks until settlement; unloading
settles waiters and handles late results. These limits bound resource use, not costs
inside the provider or the native host.

## Boundaries and residual risks

An ask is not a denial: OpenCode's client must present it and the human must evaluate it. Global auto-approve, unattended policies, saved approvals and other plugins can affect permission outcomes. Keep narrow independent hard-deny rules and the baseline shell ask rule. Do not use global auto-approve with this workflow.

Inspection commands are not side-effect-free under arbitrary environments. A replaced executable, shell alias/function, startup file, Git helper/fsmonitor, hostile repository config or compromised dependency may execute code. The plugin does not inspect executable content or enforce a filesystem/network boundary. It rejects workdir symlink components and checks canonical containment and directory identity, but cannot prevent time-of-check/time-of-use changes. It does not stop sensitive command output from reaching the primary agent. Protect secrets and enforce actual isolation separately where needed.

The shell source snapshot is correlated through native tool hooks. A tool with a different schema, custom permission assertions or unavailable source information asks. Other plugins that change source after evaluation, replace native tools or overwrite permissions are trusted code and can invalidate assumptions. A plugin load failure leaves only native rules; use ask as the baseline.

The current text API has no provider-enforced system/data split or JSON-schema output parameter. Delimiters alone cannot defeat prompt injection. The independent local grammar and policy bound potential automatic approvals even when the reviewer is compromised. They do not establish command safety in an untrusted host.

The SDK's local Promise adapter currently ignores generation cancellation options. The native smoke with a controlled loopback HTTP provider observed zero provider abort events after deadlines and reload. Timed-out calls can continue incurring costs. Eight stuck tasks exhaust active review capacity until settlement or reload. Project reviews wait only within bounded queue limits and deadlines; inspection overload asks immediately. Context history is fetched locally in full because the native endpoint lacks a limit; only local scanning and transmitted labels are bounded.

The sensitive-data tripwire is heuristic. The default closed command vocabulary and label-only context avoid forwarding arbitrary supplied strings; opt-in stateful review additionally discloses selected file contents, but a user must still trust their model provider, native provider hooks/diagnostics and OpenCode configuration. Audit sinks outside this plugin may have their own retention policies. Correlation holds temporary tool input references in bounded memory until tool completion, later pruning, or unload; audit logging persists captured commands by default until the operator removes or rotates the audit file.

Only shell permission events are protected. Direct terminals, arbitrary plugin code, MCP tools, alternate execution mechanisms and permissions that OpenCode does not emit are outside scope. The plugin never calls `permission.reply`, launches a shell, or retries an execution.

## Contracts used

`Plugin.define` accepts an id and setup function. Setup receives native options and can return async cleanup. Hook registration returns an object with async `dispose()`.

Permission evaluation exposes readonly session ID, optional agent, action, resource array, optional generic metadata and tool source, plus mutable effect and optional message. The source includes tool message and call identifiers. The hook runs after configured rules, before execution or publishing a request. It handles allow/ask; explicit configured deny skips it. Its message is used in escalated prompts/denials. The public SDK does not promise a full shell script in metadata.

Shell resources are scanner-produced strings; compounds may yield several. Consequently resources alone cannot establish the original script or operators. We observe `tool.hook("execute.before")` for the native shell tool, retain its input reference by the native source identifiers, and remove it on execute.after. Only a single scanner resource identical to a closed-grammar complete command may proceed to review. This avoids relying on undocumented metadata or guessing what the scanner omitted. ## Workflow contracts

Hybrid uses the existing stateless generation protocol for eligible inspections,
without evidence acquisition. It uses the stateful protocol for other eligible
commands and never retries an inspection decision through the project path.
Both paths preserve independently configured restrictions; hybrid inspection
conservatively treats every candidate as potentially reading the workspace and
executing a process for `forbiddenEffects`. Explicit stateful behavior and the
default stateless strategy remain distinct.

The local engine schedules at most eight active or still-unsettled tasks, with
FIFO project waiters (32 global/eight per session). Admission skips busy sessions
without skipping older work within that session. The deadline begins at gate entry;
queued expiry makes zero generation calls. A task retains its active slot/session
lock until underlying source/context/evidence/generation/recheck work settles,
even after timeout. This requires no new SDK methods or cancellation guarantees.

# Generic stateful project review

Stateful mode lets the reviewer investigate a complete shell command using bounded
project evidence, regardless of build tool or programming language. There are no
Make/Bash parsers, command allowlists, phony requirements or trusted recipe steps.
The model judges execution semantics. Local code enforces source correlation,
configured disclosure, observable command restrictions, budgets, response validation
and evidence freshness. It does not prove arbitrary programs safe or isolate them.

Stateless inspection remains the default. These options require version 0.2.0
or later (or a local build). Merge this into plugin options alongside `model`:

```json
{
  "mode": "balanced",
  "systemPrompt": "Investigate relevant build files and imported scripts. Ask when dependencies or effects are unclear.",
  "review": {
    "strategy": "stateful",
    "maxModelCalls": 4,
    "allowShellSyntax": false,
    "alwaysAsk": [],
    "forbiddenEffects": [
      "network",
      "privilege",
      "destructive",
      "outside_project",
      "unknown"
    ],
    "project": {
      "allowFileContents": true,
      "allowedPaths": ["."],
      "excludedPaths": ["private", "artifacts"],
      "maxFileBytes": 16384,
      "maxTotalBytes": 65536,
      "maxFiles": 16,
      "maxDirectoryEntries": 128
    }
  }
}
```

`allowFileContents: true` explicitly permits disclosure of requested file contents
within `allowedPaths` to the configured provider. `.` covers the project, subject
to exclusions and limits. Narrow it to specific files or directory prefixes if
needed. Paths are literal prefixes, not globs. All supplied project content is
untrusted evidence, including README files and embedded agent instructions.

## Review loop

The plugin starts with a scoped root directory listing. The reviewer can request
one full-file read, directory listing, or recursive literal-text search per model
call, then return a structured final decision. Each call uses the existing native
stateless text API with the accumulated evidence; there is no provider agent,
execution tool, MCP server or provider-side persistent conversation.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  C[Correlated complete command and project-local workdir] --> P[Local command and disclosure policy]
  P --> O[Bounded root directory overview]
  O --> M[Reviewer model]
  M -->|read, list, search| F[Validate scope and gather bounded evidence]
  F --> M
  M -->|decision| V[Validate JSON, effects, references and uncertainty]
  V --> R[Recheck native input and all inspected evidence]
  R --> A[Allow or native manual approval]
```

Ninja, CMake, Meson, Bazel, Python, Ruby, Node and unfamiliar executables follow
this same path. The model must request relevant evidence and judge dependencies;
there is no executable-name inference that a command is safe. Dynamic imports,
generated code, environment-dependent behavior, package dependencies or missing
files may prevent a sufficient review and require `ask`.

Every allow must reference at least one successful full-file read from the current
request. Listings, search snippets and previous findings alone cannot authorize
execution. This is a minimum evidence requirement, not proof that the model chose
all relevant files. A malicious or mistaken model can still approve a harmful command.

## Local controls and budgets

| Option                               | Default     | Contract                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `review.strategy`                    | `stateless` | `stateless`, `stateful`, or opt-in `hybrid` routing             |
| `review.maxModelCalls`               | `4`         | Total model calls per evaluation, 1–8, including final decision |
| `review.allowShellSyntax`            | `false`     | Permit raw shell syntax to reach model review                   |
| `review.alwaysAsk`                   | `[]`        | Case-sensitive literal command substrings that force ask        |
| `review.forbiddenEffects`            | see example | Reject model-declared effects in this list                      |
| `review.project.allowFileContents`   | `false`     | Required explicit disclosure consent                            |
| `review.project.allowedPaths`        | `["."]`     | Project-relative files/directory prefixes available as evidence |
| `review.project.excludedPaths`       | `[]`        | Additional prefixes excluded from evidence                      |
| `review.project.maxFileBytes`        | `16384`     | Per-file limit, 1–65536 bytes                                   |
| `review.project.maxTotalBytes`       | `65536`     | Aggregate unique file bytes, 1–262144                           |
| `review.project.maxFiles`            | `16`        | Unique files and, separately, directories, each limited to 1–32 |
| `review.project.maxDirectoryEntries` | `128`       | Total entries examined across unique directories, 1–512         |

Choosing `hybrid` requires the same disclosure consent. Eligible inspections with
one matching complete source/resource use the stateless reviewer without acquiring
project evidence. Its prompt includes command, matching resources, relative workdir
and optional fixed intent labels. Other eligible commands use this evidence protocol. Inspection
ask/error/malformed response/timeout never retries through project review.
`alwaysAsk` applies to both hybrid paths. Forbidding `workspace_read` or
`process_execution` conservatively blocks every hybrid inspection locally, including
`pwd`; no model declaration can override this check. Other forbidden effects retain
the closed inspection grammar and its documented trusted-environment assumptions.
Evidence path scopes apply to project acquisition; stateless inspection does not
read project files through the plugin or inherit the full-file evidence requirement.
See [the explicit development example](../examples/opencode-development.jsonc).

Choosing `stateful` applies this protocol to every eligible shell request, including
inspection commands; `stateless` retains the original inspection-only behavior.

Lists accept up to 32 entries of at most 300 characters. Paths must use ordinary
ASCII letters/numbers, spaces, underscores, dots, hyphens or slashes, without
absolute paths, empty components or `.`/`..` components (except root `.`).
Excluded scopes cannot be widened by the model. Navigation may list ancestors of
allowed prefixes, but exposes only entries leading to permitted paths.

Built-in exclusions cover `.git`, `node_modules`, `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`,
`.codex`, `.agents`, common credential filenames, and sensitive-name matches.
Symlinked paths, special files, invalid UTF-8, binary/control content and sensitive
content matches are unavailable. Secret detection is heuristic, not a guarantee;
do not grant disclosure access to confidential project areas.

Reads return whole files or an explicit unavailable result, never truncated text.
Search is literal, recursive to depth 16, and examines only permitted text files.
It returns at most 32 matching lines of at most 300 characters; overruns are
unavailable, not silently truncated. Directory listings and searches explicitly
state that their scope is permitted paths only. Excluded entries are not disclosed;
all encountered entries still count against traversal limits.

The default shell tripwire rejects backslashes, newlines, `;`, `&`, `|`, backticks,
`$`, redirection characters, parentheses and braces anywhere in the raw command.
This intentionally over-rejects some quoted arguments. It is not a shell parser or
proof against indirect execution. `allowShellSyntax: true` delegates those commands
to model review too. Commands are bounded to 8192 characters; command plus scanner
fragments to 16384 characters and 32 scanner fragments at most. An empty
resource list asks. Sensitive-data tripwires run before any command disclosure.
`alwaysAsk` also applies to eligible inspection commands in stateful mode.

The native working directory may be the project root or a project subdirectory.
The plugin resolves the canonical project root, rejects external locations, invalid
directories and symlink components, and rechecks directory identity before allow.
A symlinked project root is supported using its canonical identity. Native `~`
and `~/…` workdirs ask before evidence acquisition: OpenCode expands these against
the host home directory, while ordinary path resolution would treat them as
literal project directory names. Use an explicit project-relative or absolute path. The reviewer
receives the actual project-relative workdir (for example `packages/app`); all
evidence paths, exclusions and allowed scopes remain project-root-relative.
Embedded `cd` remains part of the command and follows shell-syntax policy.
Missing native source correlation asks. Scanner fragments can be multiple or different
from the complete command; the complete native input is always supplied and
rechecked. The model never reconstructs a command from scanner fragments.

`timeoutMs` starts at permission evaluation entry and covers source/directory
validation, queue waiting, context, overview, evidence, generation and final checks.
At most eight active or still-unsettled tasks are admitted per plugin instance.
Project reviews wait FIFO per session, capped at 32 waiting requests globally and
eight per session. Busy sessions do not block admissible work in other sessions.
Queue overflow asks with `review_queue_full` or `session_queue_full`. Source and
resources are revalidated before queued work starts. Expired waiters ask without
starting generation and are removed immediately.

A timed-out provider, context or filesystem operation retains its capacity slot
and session lock until it settles, even after the permission result is ask.
Late replies cannot allow or update findings; late rejections are handled. Unload
settles waiters as ask and clears queues. No further model calls start after cancellation.

## Protocol and approval

Evidence requests have exactly one of these shapes:

```json
{"action":"read","path":"build.ninja"}
{"action":"list","path":"src"}
{"action":"search","path":"src","query":"import helper"}
```

The final response has this shape:

```json
{
  "action": "decide",
  "decision": "allow",
  "riskLevel": "low",
  "reasonCode": "understood_operation",
  "confidence": 0.99,
  "uncertain": false,
  "evidence": ["e2"],
  "effects": ["workspace_read", "process_execution"]
}
```

Effects are `workspace_read`, `workspace_write`, `process_execution`, `network`,
`privilege`, `destructive`, `outside_project`, and `unknown`. Reason codes are
`understood_operation`, `incomplete_evidence`, `uncertain_effects`,
`suspicious_instruction`, and `restricted_effect`.

Allow requires low risk, `uncertain: false`, `understood_operation`, no forbidden
effects, no `unknown` effect, valid evidence references including a current full
read, and confidence at least 0.98/0.90/0.80 for strict/balanced/permissive modes.
These are declared model judgments. A false declaration can evade semantic
restrictions; `forbiddenEffects` does not enforce filesystem or network isolation.
Use native hard denies and actual host isolation where required.

Duplicate fields (including escaped names), extra fields, nested objects, unknown
actions/effects, invalid paths and malformed JSON ask. Replies are bounded to 4096
characters. Repeating an evidence request asks with `evidence_no_progress`.
Unavailable requested evidence always prevents allow, even if a later response
ignores it. No decision within the call budget produces `review_budget`.

All inspected file contents and visible directory inventories are rechecked before
accepting a decision. File or inventory changes produce `project_changed`. Input,
workdir or resource changes produce `input_changed` or missing-source fallback.
The recheck has its own instance of the same aggregate inspection limits, so total
filesystem work is bounded to an inspection pass and a verification pass.

## Session state and audit

Memory retains up to eight structured findings per session: effect/risk/reason
categories, a local complete-command/workdir hash and the relative workdir, and evidence paths/fingerprints. Up to 32 sessions are retained, expiring
five minutes from their first retained finding, checked on subsequent reviews.
Provider prose, command history and file contents are not stored between reviews.
Sessions are scoped to one project/plugin instance and its model/configuration.

Previous file paths can guide discovery within the same workdir, but prior findings are withheld until
the complete-command/workdir hash matches and all referenced evidence has been freshly
acquired and matches its fingerprints.
Known changed evidence invalidates the associated findings. Every command still
requires a fresh model decision. Unload clears all state; there is no approval cache.

Audit adds selected `reviewPath` (`inspection` or `project`), `queueWaitMs`, `reviewCalls`, `evidenceCount`, and validated `reviewerReasonCode` to
reviewer decision/risk metadata. Fixed local codes distinguish unavailable,
sensitive or oversized evidence, no progress, call budgets, invalid references,
changed evidence and policy escalation. Audit records include native session IDs and, by default, exact captured commands
(which may contain paths or secrets). Set `logging.includeCommands: false` to omit
command text. Evidence queries, file contents and provider prose are not logged.

## Expanded trust boundary

This strategy intentionally replaces the old Make/Bash subset verifier. Local
policy constrains evidence access and approval conditions, while the reviewer
judges arbitrary program semantics. The two former Make parsing mismatches are
retained as full-command/full-file evidence fixtures, not as claims that local
code can independently detect every dangerous Makefile.

The plugin never executes a command to inspect a project. It does not resolve
all transitive execution dependencies, validate executable binaries, inspect
runtime environments, enforce filesystem/network boundaries, or close the final
check/run race. Project prompt injection, model mistakes, host configuration,
startup files, dependencies and other plugins remain relevant risks. Raw history
and environment values are never sent, but opted-in file disclosure can reveal
private data not caught by the heuristic tripwire.

Stateless inspection retains its closed grammar. Explicit native denies and
non-shell permissions are preserved in both strategies. Errors, uncertainty,
missing source, unresolved evidence failures, timeout, overload and unload ask.
